evidence: app/package.json:11-13 — typescript ^7.0.2 and vite ^8.3.5, both the current stable releases as of 2026-10 (verified against npm registry and vite.dev/releases)
app/src/main.ts:74-96 — hand-rolled pushState/popstate SPA router, still the standard vanilla pattern
app/vite.config.ts:1-5 — defineConfig, no deprecated vite options
latest_apis.rationale: Consistently on the current generation of Vite and TypeScript with zero legacy APIs, but the code itself doesn't adopt any newer-than-mainstream API that would distinguish it.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:184-200 — fetch with a promise-cache, no hand-rolled HTTP
app/src/pages/home.ts:13-19 — URLSearchParams for filter state in the URL
app/src/components.ts:49 — loading="lazy" + intrinsic width/height on sprites
app/src/components.ts:49 — inline onerror attribute, the one CSP-unfriendly hand-rolled touch
platform.rationale: Reaches for the platform first (fetch, URL, ESM, native form controls, CSS grid/custom properties); the inline event handler and string-concatenated HTML are the only non-modern fallbacks.

evidence: app/package.json:10-13 — zero runtime dependencies; only typescript and vite as devDependencies
app/server.mjs:1-4 — static server built on node:http/node:fs, no express/sirv
dependencies.rationale: Minimal and modern: no runtime packages at all, and the two devDependencies are both the latest stable releases.

evidence: app/src/api.ts:184-379 — all data access, response types, normalization and caching behind one module
app/src/api.ts:1-6 — API base URL resolved in a single place (injected config, then env, then default)
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:144 — apiFetch<any> bypasses the typed boundary
app/src/pages/pokemon.ts:112 — route duplicated inline instead of reusing speciesHref (components.ts:14)
app/src/components.ts:3-11 — manual escapeHtml; every template site must remember to escape
churn_resistance.rationale: Data, config and routing are each isolated so framework or API moves touch few files; the string-template-with-manual-escaping pattern and a couple of boundary leaks are where future churn will concentrate.

findings.issue: All markup is built by string concatenation with a hand-rolled escapeHtml; every new interpolated value relies on a developer remembering to escape, so future fields are a per-site XSS/rendering churn risk.
findings.suggestion: Introduce a tagged-template html`...` helper that auto-escapes interpolations (or build DOM via <template>), so safety is structural rather than per-call.

findings.issue: Inline onerror="this.style.visibility='hidden'" fails under a CSP without unsafe-inline and is the only non-declarative bit of the card.
findings.suggestion: Hide broken sprites via a delegated capture-phase 'error' listener in main.ts, or a CSS fallback on the wrapper.

findings.issue: apiFetch<any> for move records discards the typed API boundary the rest of the app maintains.
findings.suggestion: Type it as apiFetch<MoveRecord> and reuse the existing record interface, keeping type drift detectable.

findings.issue: The evolution link builds /pokemon/${encodeURIComponent(...)} inline, duplicating speciesHref in components.ts.
findings.suggestion: Import and use speciesHref so route changes stay in one place.

findings.issue: TypeScript is installed but no script ever runs it (vite build doesn't typecheck), so type errors can drift silently.
findings.suggestion: Add a "typecheck": "tsc --noEmit" script (tsc 7 is the fast native compiler) and wire it into build.

summary: A lean, current-gen vanilla TS + Vite app: zero runtime dependencies, latest stable Vite 8 and native TypeScript 7, and all data access, config and routing isolated to single modules, which keeps upgrade churn low. The main forward-looking liability is the string-template rendering with manual escaping plus one apiFetch<any> leak at an otherwise well-typed boundary. Nothing legacy or deprecated is in use, so future framework releases would touch few files.
